title: OOP Principles in Java
summary: Java OOP rests on four ideas: encapsulation hides state behind methods, inheritance reuses behavior via 'extends', polymorphism lets one call resolve to different implementations at runtime, and abstraction exposes only what a caller needs through interfaces or abstract classes.
example: Prefer composition over inheritance when a class needs to reuse behavior from more than one source — e.g. a PaymentService that both logs and validates shouldn't extend two base classes, it should hold a Logger and a Validator.
mistakes: Confusing overloading (compile-time, same class) with overriding (runtime, subclass) — interviewers ask this constantly.
Making every field 'protected' instead of 'private' — that isn't encapsulation, it just moves the leak up one level.
followUps: How does Java achieve runtime polymorphism, and what role does the vtable / dynamic dispatch play?
When would you reach for an interface instead of an abstract class?
